# OBS recording runtime source information

This directory is a separate recording-runtime inventory for OpenCam 1.0.0 preparation. It does not replace the standalone media-tool notices or claim completed device acceptance. The assembler initially sets `runtime.json.enabled` to `false`; the validated packaging workflow controls activation. Exact built-source provenance belongs in the package's SOURCE.txt and runtime manifest, not a claim inferred from this document's version.

OBS 33.0.0 source is pinned to `72e86655715d9a25d69ce446aa4dd44ba58e10d2`. The Apple DMG SHA-256 is recorded in `inventory.json`; it was verified against the official GitHub release asset metadata. Frameworks and plugin binaries are copied unchanged from the read-only mounted official bundle. The newly built helper alone receives a local runtime rpath and ad hoc signature in its staging copy. macOS uses standard `Contents/MacOS/OpenCam.ObsCapture` layout with an owned `Contents/Info.plist` identity `org.opencam.recordingcore`, `LSUIElement`, and microphone usage description. The rpath is `@loader_path/../Frameworks`. Application initialization tests need access to the normal user LaunchServices context; the command sandbox blocks AppKit registration before device capture.

The upstream source includes a dependency lock in `CMakePresets.json`: OBS deps release `2026-10-23`, source commit `cbf0a3d8a0a34c07e822bda22a5f8214f91801d7`, macOS universal archive SHA-256 `6ded92c5d97f1d1b5effa07be13cc9f539826aa9c65013a15872328e39acffbf`. Source, dependency versions, build options, and required OBS dependency patches are available at:

- https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/tree/72e86655715d9a25d69ce446aa4dd44ba58e10d2
- https://github.com/obsproject/obs-deps/tree/cbf0a3d8a0a34c07e822bda22a5f8214f91801d7
- https://github.com/obsproject/obs-deps/tree/cbf0a3d8a0a34c07e822bda22a5f8214f91801d7/deps.ffmpeg
- https://github.com/obsproject/obs-deps/tree/cbf0a3d8a0a34c07e822bda22a5f8214f91801d7/deps.ffmpeg/patches

`inventory.json` identifies individual source revisions and full license/attribution files. The official Windows and macOS runtime libavutil binaries identify n8.1.2 (`38b88335f99e76ed89ff3c93f877fdefce736c13`), matching the pinned dependency recipes. Both configure strings enable GPL and version3. FFmpeg helper headers separately use n8.1.3 (`1041abdc962f4cc4f394aa8de9dc5236c0c3b9e7`); SIMDe headers use v0.8.2 (`71fd833d9666141edcd1d3c109a80e228303d8d7`). Header pins do not substitute for runtime source. The GPL FFmpeg build includes x264 and static aom, Theora, LAME, Opus, Vorbis and VPX, with Ogg as a codec dependency; Windows additionally includes SVT-AV1. Their retained nested notices are included. librist/SRT/Mbed TLS are loader dependencies even though OpenCam loads no streaming modules or network outputs. Apple system frameworks and `/usr/lib` libraries are supplied by macOS and are not copied.

macOS roots are `libobs.framework`, `libobs-metal.dylib`, `libobs-opengl.dylib`, plus only `obs-x264`, `obs-ffmpeg`, `mac-capture`, `mac-videotoolbox`, and optional `coreaudio-encoder` plugin bundles. Only the explicit framework allowlist may satisfy their recursive load commands. Framework aliases are dereferenced within the official source root; the staged tree contains only regular files and directories. No CEF, Qt, OBS frontend, browser, websocket, game injection, or streaming plugin is packaged.

Windows staging normalizes official OBS 33 `core/<module>/<module>.dll` and `core/<module>/data` into the private `obs-plugins/64bit` and `data/obs-plugins` layout, with required `obs.dll`/D3D11/WinRT/core data. Selected official modules are `obs-x264`, `obs-ffmpeg`, `win-wasapi` and optional `obs-nvenc`, `obs-qsv11`. The full upstream `win-capture` is never packaged: its module entry initializes game hooks and a compatibility updater. OpenCam instead compiles only the pinned `duplicator-monitor-capture.c`, `cursor-capture.c` and its own `windows-display-module.c`; the assembler requires that built display-only DLL. Only capture translations are copied; game injection binaries and configuration are excluded.

The pinned Windows x64 AMF implementation resides in `obs-ffmpeg`. NVIDIA/QSV/AMD require their exact `obs-nvenc-test.exe`/`obs-qsv-test.exe`/`obs-amf-test.exe` at the helper executable root and are not advertised when those probes are absent. The caller constructs child PATH using only validated runtime `bin/64bit` and Windows SystemDirectory before starting the helper; native DLL-directory initialization happens too late for initial PE imports. Windows packages carry authenticated app-local Microsoft release CRT files beside the helper and GPU probes. Their original signatures, file versions, hashes, provenance and full Visual Studio 2022 license are retained in the runtime inventory. No SystemDirectory DLL is copied and no separate runtime installation is required. CI inspects actual loaded CRT module paths to ensure hosted system copies do not mask a missing bundled file.

`scripts/prepare-obs-validation.mjs` verifies the official GitHub asset API and ZIP digest, checks out all four exact source revisions, and assembles a separate Windows notice inventory, including GPL-3.0-or-later FFmpeg and the statically included codec dependencies. The Windows ZIP SHA-256 is `3369a3ecd67b5669a8a08d77357f87cc786d1fba42fbbd1054d841a69f6271a7`. Its lock also records the known configure-generated public FFmpeg header; copying it requires verified n8.1.3 source and the exact two-option public configuration contract. No FFmpeg binary is built by that step. This macOS inventory must not be reused for Windows. The isolated `verify-obs-core.yml` workflow runs only on the validation branch (or manual dispatch selecting that branch), retains disabled manifests and diagnostics, and makes no Release/deployment writes. Physical recording and long-duration acceptance remain separate requirements.

To reproduce a development build, provide clean pinned Git checkouts and a new build directory to `scripts/build-obs-capture.sh` (or the PowerShell wrapper on Windows). To stage, append a new destination and this notice directory. The assembler rejects existing destinations and computes SHA-256 after helper relocation. Never add or modify staged files without rebuilding the whole manifest; the managed selector rejects unlisted or changed files.

Source delivery uses `node scripts/collect-obs-corresponding-sources.mjs NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`, producing `OBS-SOURCES.tar.gz` and `OBS-SOURCES.json`. `scripts/obs-corresponding-sources.lock.json` pins full runtime and header source inputs separately, plus unchanged upstream download archives and checksums. The collector includes all tracked obs-deps recipes, utilities and vendored patch files; recursively captures dependency gitlinks with an extraction/restoration map; and explicitly excludes the unused OBS DirectShow, browser and websocket submodules. Supplied Git checkouts require exact HEAD and clean tracked files. Supplied archive bytes require the pinned SHA-256. A failed acquisition produces no completed manifest or bundle. Optional `OPENCAM_OBS_SOURCE_DIRECTORIES` is a JSON object mapping source ids to local pinned checkouts; `OPENCAM_OBS_SOURCE_ARCHIVES` names a directory containing every archive under its lock filename.

Before distribution, preserve this corresponding source bundle and the matching OpenCam helper source/build tree alongside the binary distribution. The inventory and generated manifests are source provenance audits, not a legal compliance determination. Upstream links alone are not the source delivery artifact.
